import sys
from collections import defaultdict

EPS = 1e-9


def cross(ax, ay, bx, by):
    return ax * by - ay * bx


def on_segment(a, b, p):
    ax, ay = a
    bx, by = b
    px, py = p
    if abs(cross(bx - ax, by - ay, px - ax, py - ay)) > EPS:
        return False
    return (min(ax, bx) - EPS <= px <= max(ax, bx) + EPS and
            min(ay, by) - EPS <= py <= max(ay, by) + EPS)


def segment_overlap_positive(a, b, c, d):
    # Returns True iff collinear segments AB and CD overlap with positive length
    ax, ay = a
    bx, by = b
    cx, cy = c
    dx, dy = d

    # Must be collinear
    if abs(cross(bx - ax, by - ay, cx - ax, cy - ay)) > EPS:
        return False
    if abs(cross(bx - ax, by - ay, dx - ax, dy - ay)) > EPS:
        return False

    # Project to dominant axis
    if abs(ax - bx) >= abs(ay - by):
        l1, r1 = sorted((ax, bx))
        l2, r2 = sorted((cx, dx))
    else:
        l1, r1 = sorted((ay, by))
        l2, r2 = sorted((cy, dy))

    overlap = min(r1, r2) - max(l1, l2)
    return overlap > EPS


def polygons_adjacent(poly1, poly2):
    n1 = len(poly1)
    n2 = len(poly2)
    for i in range(n1):
        a = poly1[i]
        b = poly1[(i + 1) % n1]
        for j in range(n2):
            c = poly2[j]
            d = poly2[(j + 1) % n2]
            if segment_overlap_positive(a, b, c, d):
                return True
    return False


def build_country_graph(countries):
    names = list(countries.keys())
    m = len(names)
    adj = [0] * m

    for i in range(m):
        polys_i = countries[names[i]]
        for j in range(i + 1, m):
            polys_j = countries[names[j]]
            ok = False
            for p1 in polys_i:
                for p2 in polys_j:
                    if polygons_adjacent(p1, p2):
                        ok = True
                        break
                if ok:
                    break
            if ok:
                adj[i] |= 1 << j
                adj[j] |= 1 << i
    return adj


def chromatic_number(adj):
    n = len(adj)
    if n <= 1:
        return n

    degrees = [adj[i].bit_count() for i in range(n)]
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: -degrees[x])

    new_index = [0] * n
    for ni, old in enumerate(order):
        new_index[old] = ni

    radj = [0] * n
    for old_u in range(n):
        u = new_index[old_u]
        mask = adj[old_u]
        while mask:
            b = mask & -mask
            old_v = b.bit_length() - 1
            v = new_index[old_v]
            radj[u] |= 1 << v
            mask ^= b

    adj = radj
    degrees = [adj[i].bit_count() for i in range(n)]

    best = n

    color_masks = []

    def greedy_upper_bound():
        colors = []
        for v in range(n):
            placed = False
            for c in range(len(colors)):
                if (adj[v] & colors[c]) == 0:
                    colors[c] |= 1 << v
                    placed = True
                    break
            if not placed:
                colors.append(1 << v)
        return len(colors)

    best = greedy_upper_bound()

    def color_bound(uncolored):
        # Greedy coloring of induced subgraph gives upper bound on clique in complement,
        # used here as a pruning lower bound on needed additional colors.
        # Returns number of colors used in greedy coloring of remaining vertices.
        cnt = 0
        rem = uncolored
        while rem:
            cnt += 1
            available = rem
            chosen = 0
            while available:
                b = available & -available
                v = b.bit_length() - 1
                chosen |= b
                available &= ~b
                available &= ~adj[v]
            rem &= ~chosen
        return cnt

    def dfs(colored_count, used_colors, uncolored):
        nonlocal best
        if used_colors >= best:
            return
        if uncolored == 0:
            best = used_colors
            return

        lb = color_bound(uncolored)
        if used_colors + max(1, (lb + 3) // 4) >= best:
            # Since planar maps need at most 4 colors, this weak compression helps a bit.
            pass

        # Choose vertex with maximum saturation/degree heuristic approximation:
        # here simply highest degree among uncolored.
        temp = uncolored
        v = -1
        best_deg = -1
        while temp:
            b = temp & -temp
            u = b.bit_length() - 1
            if degrees[u] > best_deg:
                best_deg = degrees[u]
                v = u
            temp ^= b

        # Try existing colors
        for c in range(used_colors):
            if (adj[v] & color_masks[c]) == 0:
                color_masks[c] |= 1 << v
                dfs(colored_count + 1, used_colors, uncolored & ~(1 << v))
                color_masks[c] &= ~(1 << v)

        # Try new color
        color_masks.append(1 << v)
        dfs(colored_count + 1, used_colors + 1, uncolored & ~(1 << v))
        color_masks.pop()

    dfs(0, 0, (1 << n) - 1)
    return best


def parse_input(tokens):
    idx = 0
    cases = []
    while idx < len(tokens):
        t = int(tokens[idx])
        idx += 1
        if t == 0:
            break
        countries = defaultdict(list)
        for _ in range(t):
            name = tokens[idx]
            idx += 1
            k = int(tokens[idx])
            idx += 1
            poly = []
            for _ in range(k):
                x = float(tokens[idx])
                y = float(tokens[idx + 1])
                idx += 2
                poly.append((x, y))
            countries[name].append(poly)
        cases.append(countries)
    return cases


def main():
    tokens = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not tokens:
        return

    cases = parse_input(tokens)
    out = []
    for countries in cases:
        adj = build_country_graph(countries)
        ans = chromatic_number(adj)
        out.append(str(ans))
    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
